paper.title: Quantum Algorithm for Online Exp-concave Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Online exp-concave optimization with quantum zeroth-order oracle (smooth losses)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Quantum oracle access: feedback is a quantum zeroth-order oracle queried in superposition.
unmapped: losses are alpha-exp-concave (alpha_exp); the learner knows alpha_exp
feedback is a quantum zeroth-order oracle (unitary) queried O(1) times per round with superposition inputs
completely adaptive adversary that picks f_t after observing x_t
settings.definition_quote: We assume the loss functions are $\alpha$-exp-concave and G-Lipschitz continuous... the feasible set $\mathcal{K}$ is bounded and its diameter has an upper bound $D$... $\mathcal{K},D,G$ are known to the player... the loss functions are assumed to be $\beta$-smooth directly.

settings.name_in_paper: Online exp-concave optimization with quantum zeroth-order oracle (non-smooth losses)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Quantum oracle access: feedback is a quantum zeroth-order oracle queried in superposition.
unmapped: losses are alpha-exp-concave (alpha_exp); the learner knows alpha_exp
feedback is a quantum zeroth-order oracle queried O(1) times per round with superposition inputs
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we present how to extend Algorithm \ref{QONS} to non-smooth loss functions.

settings.name_in_paper: Online exp-concave optimization with gradient and Hessian feedback
unmapped: learner also observes the Hessian of f_t at x_t (second-order feedback)
losses twice differentiable and satisfy f(y) >= f(x) + grad f(x)^T(y-x) + (eta/2)(y-x)^T H(f)(x)(y-x) (Hessian-based exp-concavity-like condition)
settings.definition_quote: We still study the online exp-concave optimization problem, but assume here the player can get the gradient and the Hessian of the loss function in each round efficiently after suffering the loss... We assume that the gradient of the loss functions is $L$-Lipschitz continuous... we further assume that $\forall x,y \in \mathcal{K}, f_t(y) \geq f_t(x) + \nabla f_t(x)^{\mathrm{T}}(y-x)+\frac{\eta}{2}(y-x)^{\mathrm{T}} H(f_t)(x) (y-x)$

algorithms.name: Non-smooth version of QONS (random smoothing point z_t)
Online Newton Method with Hessian Update

symbols.rho: per-round failure probability of quantum gradient estimation

conditions: quantum zeroth-order oracle, O(1) queries per round
tuning: r_t = rho G / (pi n^3 (n/rho+1) beta t)

source.label: TNQ
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{QONS} with parameters $\eta=\min\left\{\frac{1}{8GD},\frac{\alpha}{2}\right\}$, $\epsilon=\frac{1}{\eta^2 D^2}$, $\left\{r_t=\frac{\rho G}{\pi n^3 (n/\rho +1) \beta t}\right\}_{t=1}^T$, can achieve the regret bound $O\left(\left(DG+\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)n\log(T+\log T)\right)$ with probability greater than $1-T\rho$, and its query complexity is $O(1)$ in each round.

results.notes: Probability 1 - T*rho; delta = T*rho. Theorem number inferred from mythe counter (first theorem). n mapped to d, D to diam_K, G to L_lip. Horizon marked known since rho is set via delta/T.

symbols.alpha_exp: exp-concavity parameter (used as grad grad^T <= H/alpha in proof)

conditions: f_t(y) >= f_t(x) + grad^T(y-x) + (eta/2)(y-x)^T H(y-x) for all x,y
gradient and Hessian observed each round

source.label: TNHQ
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{ONSH} with parameters $\eta=\frac{1}{2DL}$ and $\epsilon=L$, can achieve the regret bound $O\left(\frac{DLn}{\alpha}\log(T+1)\right)$.

results.notes: Deterministic bound for any loss sequence; probability type not stated ('expectation' chosen as placeholder, quantity regret_unspecified). Paper's L mapped to beta. Theorem number inferred from counter.

symbols.p_fail: per-round failure probability of local smoothness
